proposal.title: ComputerLand: 20% average margin, returnable stock and Academy shopping corners
proposal.reason: Author-directed revision of the ComputerLand and Academy sales model. Replace the existing 20–30% range with a 20% average gross margin for ComputerLand locations; combine net-90 interest-free merchant credit, on-demand replenishment and full-value stock-balancing returns so shops normally need no inventory working capital. Recognise Academy shopping corners as a parallel non-exclusive sales channel, with nearby warehouses and Logix logistics, while preserving existing training/voucher eligibility and dealer reimbursement. Keep the 1978 preparation/public launch distinct from the existing 17 July 1980 regional institutional-sales rollout. These six records form one coherent review group. The author explicitly requests the margin and credit terms in the existing agreement: this is a scoped instruction overriding the general no-pricing authoring guidance, not a general pricing-model extension. Financial terms remain in agreement clauses; no product prices, historic shop-cost estimates, invented cities, new dates or projected sales are introduced. Complete before snapshots are from main at e0e54da; no pending concrete proposal overlaps these records. Foundation and authorization records remain unchanged until Changes confirm applies this proposal.

before.title: ComputerLand retail agreement

party.role: Negotiator of the Logix retail distribution arrangement
Retail distributor receiving the agreed margin

before.description: Adam and ComputerLand arranged a primary retail channel for Logix computers. The partnership connected Logix’s hardware and software offering with an established specialist dealer network.

clauses.statement: ComputerLand receives a retailer margin in the agreed range of 20–30% on products covered by the retail distribution arrangement.

after.title: ComputerLand retail agreement

party.role: Negotiator of the Logix retail distribution arrangement
Retail distributor receiving the agreed margin

after.description: Adam and ComputerLand arrange a non-exclusive specialist retail channel for Logix computers alongside Logix Computer Academy direct sales. Logix supports participating shops with replenishment, merchant credit and stock-balancing returns, using its own logistics network and warehouses near Academy facilities. ComputerLand locations provide demonstrations, configuration advice and retail customer service.

clauses.statement: Participating ComputerLand locations receive an agreed average retailer gross margin of 20% on covered Logix computer sales, replacing the previous 20–30% range. The percentage is measured against retail sales value before sales tax, rather than as a markup on wholesale cost; commercial settlement schedules are to deliver this average across covered location sales.

Logix provides interest-free merchant credit: payment for each computer is due 90 days after the shop receives it, with no advance payment or inventory deposit. Return credits reduce the corresponding amount payable before its due date. Computers already sold remain payable on the original due date; replenishment does not restart that clock.

Participating shops may request replenishment whenever needed and manage stock to cover approximately three to four weeks of expected sales. Logix replenishes through its own logistics network according to available stock and transport schedules; the arrangement does not require shops to accept excess allocations.

Shops may return unsold computers in saleable condition whenever demand slows or stock exceeds approximately one month of expected sales, including before the 90-day invoice falls due. Logix accepts these stock-balancing returns at full invoiced value without a restocking charge and arranges collection through its logistics network. A notified return awaiting Logix collection is excluded from the payable balance until collected and credited, provided the goods remain available in saleable condition; no overdue charge arises solely from Logix collection or credit-processing delay.

Logix carries the financing and obsolescence exposure for returnable unsold inventory. With routine replenishment and timely stock-balancing returns, shops are intended to fund payment from completed customer sales rather than their own inventory capital. ComputerLand locations remain responsible for their premises, staff, demonstrations, customer service and care of stock in their custody.

As Academy facilities open, Logix provides a nearby warehouse serving each facility and moves computer supply through its own logistics network. These warehouses support Academy shopping corners, customer fulfilment, participating dealer replenishment and stock-balancing returns; warehouse provision follows facility rollout rather than implying that all sites already exist at agreement signing.

ComputerLand distribution is non-exclusive. Logix reserves direct sales through small shopping corners at Academy facilities and through its regional sales organisation. Academy shopping corners accept ordinary purchases independently of course attendance or voucher possession. Academy facilities may also house regional sales staff; the establishment of those offices follows the separately recorded rollout.

Academy facilities continue training and redemption of applicable try-before-you-buy and course-completion purchase vouchers under the existing programme rules. Eligible customers may redeem their purchase credit through Academy direct sales or participating authorised dealers. Logix reimburses dealer redemptions without reducing the agreed retailer margin; existing eligibility, validity and non-stacking rules remain in force, and training creates no obligation to purchase.

before.title: Official Logix Computer Academy launch, including SSG General Ledger training
before.description: On 16 June 1978, Logix Computer Academy launches its public programme, including Aurelia Fundamentals and SSG-authorised General Ledger courses and distribution. Teach setup, journal entry, corrections, reporting, period-end work, backup/restore and Abacus summary export. Each initial centre has access to SSG specialist help. Dealers handle installation enquiries, SSG handles application defects and accounting support, Logix supports hardware and AION supports platform tools. Courses, setup services and software licences remain separate offerings.

participant.role: authorised training and direct distribution provider

inputs.description: The combined June 6 AION C IDE and SSG General Ledger presentation releases the Aurelia port used in the courses and dealer demonstrations.
SSG’s separately licensed General Ledger for Aurelia is the application taught and distributed; the Academy does not own the accounting product.
The Academy company and its preparation of the initial five-city programme provide the organisation and facilities basis for the public launch.

outcomes.description: The Academy publicly launches hands-on Aurelia training, configuration advice and direct ordering; customer-site delivery remains an option and immediate collection depends on stock.

SSG-authorised General Ledger courses, distribution and dealer preparation begin with defined support boundaries. Plan later year-end workshops and supported-edition updates based on verified customer results.
